clue.text: Crook in e.g. Kent fearing Bill's reappearance

parts.note: Kent is a county in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
a crook is a con, a swindler
fearing means dreading

explanation.surface: A villain hiding out in the Kent countryside dreads a returning invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' just places the crook in the county's region, so the region comes first. 'Bill' is a parliamentary bill, not an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament a bill is debated again at its second reading, the stage where the proposed law returns to the chamber.

clue.text: Reduction of personnel, in decline over long period

indicators.note: the personnel department's letters sit inside the word for decline

parts.note: to decline is to sink
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A company's staff numbers falling steadily over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second, so it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is a lessening in size or amount, a synonym for reduction.

clue.text: Originally French account manager in London

definitions.meaning: a short tale, the word borrowed from French
Antonio ... managed Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur, both London football clubs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Account manager' looks like one business job; split it, and the account is a story while the manager is a football boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a short story told in French tradition and the Italian football coach who ran two London clubs.

clue.text: Opera contains English character and German aria

indicators.note: the opera's name holds the following letters within it

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S, a character of the English alphabet
und is German for 'and'

explanation.surface: An opera featuring an English role alongside a German song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and German' is one piece, the German word for 'and', not a link plus a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessun Dorma is the famous tenor aria from Puccini's Turandot, sung by Calaf.

clue.text: King heading off sycophants — Queen's helpers, say

parts.note: R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for sycophants is removed

parts.note: toadies are fawning flatterers

explanation.surface: A monarch rid of his flatterers, with the Queen's attendants nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is the rock band, not the monarch: R replaces the head of TOADIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadies are the touring crew who set up equipment for a band such as Queen, an example signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Parent with head lowered getting tot up

indicators.note: in a down entry the first letter is moved down to the bottom

parts.note: dad is a parent

explanation.surface: A father bowing his head while totting up the sums.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the top of DAD drops to the foot of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To add numbers is to total them, which is what tot up means.

clue.text: Travel in Europe and football club complain

parts.note: Inter, Internazionale of Milan, is a football club
to rail is to complain bitterly

explanation.surface: A fan's European trip ruined by griping about a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: InterRail is a rail pass for touring Europe by train, used as a verb for that kind of trip.

clue.text: Dope that is one encouraging wishful thinking?

parts.note: dope is slang for information, as is gen
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A drug that makes people daydream about what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope here means inside information, not a drug or a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie of the lamp grants wishes, so it invites the hopeful to make them, wishful thinking made real.

clue.text: Two monkeys and bear show off

parts.note: in British slang a monkey is five hundred pounds, so two make a thousand, a grand
to bear is to stand, tolerate

explanation.surface: A zoo display of a couple of apes and a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: A monkey is British slang for £500; two of them make a grand (£1,000).
explanation.definitionFit: To grandstand is to behave ostentatiously to impress onlookers, to show off.

clue.text: Small-scale return of Sex and the City

indicators.note: the word for sex is turned back to front

parts.note: it is an old euphemism for sex
NY, New York, is the city of the TV series

explanation.surface: A modest comeback for the TV show Sex and the City.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Sex' is returned; the city keeps its order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny means very small, describing something on a minute scale.

clue.text: Concerned with voguish frame of reference

parts.note: something voguish is in, fashionable

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Talking about a trendy point of reference.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is a Latin legal phrase meaning in the matter of, regarding.

clue.text: Squeal in nude tipsily in the dark

indicators.note: the word for squeal goes inside the rearranged letters
a tipsy arrangement is a drunken jumble of the letters

parts.note: to squeal is to inform on someone

explanation.surface: A drunk naked person shrieking in a darkened room.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the insertion signal; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark about something means lacking knowledge of it, uninformed.

clue.text: It could deceive in case voice, male, stifles hum

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the voice and male letters surround the hum

parts.note: falsetto is a high singing voice
hum is slang for a bad smell, and BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A man's high voice drowning out a hum, possibly a trick in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum is British slang for a bad smell, hence body odour; the case is a suitcase, not a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A false bottom is a hidden compartment in a box or suitcase, built to fool anyone searching it.

clue.text: What drug smuggler did heartlessly is foul

indicators.note: the central letter is removed, the heart of the phrase

parts.note: a smuggler ran acid, LSD, across a border

explanation.surface: A drug runner's callous dealings are disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN ACID has seven letters; its middle letter, A, goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid describes food gone bad with a rank, rotten smell, as foul does.

clue.text: Boor wanting latitude to relax: is this ideal for BoJo?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the latitude letter is dropped

parts.note: a churl is a rude, boorish person
to chill is to relax

explanation.surface: A lout lacking room to unwind, asking about Boris Johnson's ideals.
explanation.walkthrough: BoJo is Boris Johnson, the former UK prime minister, who wrote a biography of his hero Winston Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson idolised Winston Churchill, wartime prime minister, as his model statesman.

clue.text: Seconds needed after most of dessert course

indicators.note: the seconds letter is placed after the trimmed dessert
the final letter of the dessert is dropped

parts.note: syllabub is a creamy whipped dessert

explanation.surface: Wanting second helpings after nearly finishing the pudding course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a meal course; it is a course of study. A syllabub is an old English dessert of whipped cream and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of topics covered in a course of study.

clue.text: All-inclusive college has 30% leaving with advanced Latin

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters are taken away from the word for college

parts.note: a university is a college of higher learning
the word for college has ten letters, so thirty per cent is three of them, here the last three
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A college losing almost a third of its students but offering advanced Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirty per cent of a ten-letter word is exactly three letters, taken from its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to everyone or everything, which all-inclusive also expresses.

clue.text: Calls for soldiers to get bundles of sheets

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A demand that troops be issued with stacks of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The sheets are paper, not bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: If something requires a thing it needs it, as a situation calls for action.

clue.text: Teacher, around end of year, needing a cocktail

indicators.note: the teacher's letters go round the others

parts.note: sir is what pupils call a male teacher
Dec, December, is the year's last month

explanation.surface: A teacher at the close of the year, in need of a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December; DEC and A go inside SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Danes on screen bringing forth English cake

indicators.note: the English letter is brought forward to the front

parts.note: Claire Danes is a film and television actress

explanation.surface: Danish people on television producing an English pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Danes is the actress Claire Danes, not people from Denmark; her E moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Bird biting horse and wild dog, which is risky

indicators.note: the bird's letters close around the horse letter, as a beak bites

parts.note: a toucan is a tropical bird
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: wild signals the letters run loose in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird pecking at a horse and a feral dog, a dangerous scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild dog' looks like dingo, but 'wild' jumbles DOG into DGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch and go describes a precarious situation whose outcome is uncertain and dangerous.

clue.text: A little creep unworthily about to tell the truth

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards
only a small part of the words is taken, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A minor sneak behaving shabbily before coming clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, admitting honestly what one has done.

clue.text: Rogue back in Oxford, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dishonest, contemptible man
second meaning: the rear part of a shoe such as an Oxford

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe, not the city or university.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scoundrel and the raised rear part of footwear.

clue.text: Henry, turning up, eggs on Charlie to create chaos

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for eggs is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ova are eggs
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Henry arriving and urging Charlie on to cause mayhem.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc means widespread destruction and confusion, a synonym for chaos.

clue.text: Not a fan of conservationists visiting capital

indicators.note: the visitors go inside the place being visited

parts.note: A1 is first-rate, capital, written AI
NT, the National Trust, is a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the environmental group coming to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city; here it means excellent, A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning opposed to, as someone who is no fan of a thing is.

clue.text: Reporter, one aboard the tube first, is a keyboard warrior

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

indicators.note: one is aboard, so inside, the television

parts.note: the tube is slang for television, TV
I is the Roman numeral one
first is written 1st, with I for 1

explanation.surface: A journalist who boards the Underground first is an online campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tube' looks like the London Underground but is the TV; 'first' as 1ST gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacktivist breaks into computer systems for political ends, a militant fighter at the keyboard.

clue.text: Asian ruler losing lead in race in China

indicators.note: the first letter of the ruler's title is dropped

parts.note: a khan is a ruler in Central Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian ruler falls behind in a contest held in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a contest; it means an ethnic group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Han are China's majority ethnic group, named after the Han dynasty.

clue.text: Description of Anna, Eve, Bob, Otto, Viv and Carol — plain dim, unfortunately!

definitions.text: Description of Anna, Eve, Bob, Otto, Viv

indicators.note: an unfortunate result is one that went wrong, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Listing names that read the same both ways, then lamenting that Carol does not.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol is the odd one out in the list: she is not a palindrome, and she is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of those names reads identically forwards and backwards, the defining property of a palindrome.
